questions.q: Why can Lesson 7's new index degrade over time even though the fix is correct?
options: Every INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE can force page splits that gradually fragment the index, the same as any index
The index automatically deletes itself after 30 days
Azure SQL Database removes custom indexes during maintenance windows
The fix was never actually applied correctly in Lesson 7
questions.explain: Ongoing write activity against dbo.Invoices naturally fragments IX_Invoices_PatientID over time, just like any index.

questions.q: Why filter the fragmentation query to page_count > 500?
options: A small, heavily fragmented index still fits in a handful of reads, so fragmentation only matters once an index is big enough
page_count has no effect on whether fragmentation matters
Indexes under 500 pages cannot become fragmented
It is required syntax for sys.dm_db_index_physical_stats to run at all
questions.explain: Fragmentation on a tiny index barely changes read cost; it matters once the index is large enough for physical layout to affect I/O.

questions.q: In the decision script, what happens at or above 30% fragmentation?
options: ALTER INDEX ... REBUILD WITH (ONLINE = ON) runs — thorough, heavier, but non-blocking
The index is dropped and never recreated
Nothing — only REORGANIZE ever runs regardless of fragmentation level
The entire database is taken offline
questions.explain: At or above the 30% threshold, the script runs a full online REBUILD rather than the lighter REORGANIZE.

questions.q: What real-world DBA tooling does this REBUILD/REORGANIZE logic mirror?
options: Ola Hallengren's widely-used Maintenance Solution
SQL Server Agent's built-in alert system
Azure Monitor's metric dashboards
The missing-index DMVs from Lesson 6
questions.explain: This decision logic mirrors the real, widely-adopted community-standard maintenance solution rather than something invented from scratch.

questions.q: Why doesn't running the maintenance script once solve the problem long-term?
options: The index will fragment again the moment real write traffic resumes, which happens every business day
The script can only be run one time per Azure subscription
Running it twice would corrupt the index permanently
Fragmentation never recurs once it has been fixed a single time
questions.explain: Ongoing daily write activity means fragmentation returns, so this needs a recurring schedule, not a one-time run.
